concept.body: A square is simultaneously a rectangle (four right angles) and a rhombus (four congruent sides), so it inherits BOTH property sets with nothing extra to memorize: congruent diagonals (rectangle), perpendicular angle-bisecting diagonals (rhombus), mutual bisection (parallelogram). Each corner's 90° splits into 45° halves, making the diagonal s√2.

explanationVariants: Perpendicular diagonals reach the square through its RHOMBUS parentage — equal sides are what force the 90° crossing.
The rectangle parent contributes congruent diagonals; perpendicularity rides in with the rhombus genes.

widget.prompt: A square's diagonals are perpendicular. Which parent supplies that property?

options.label: The rhombus side of the family (all sides congruent)
options.feedback: Perpendicular, angle-bisecting diagonals are the rhombus signature — the square inherits them via its equal sides.

options.label: The rectangle side of the family (all right angles)
options.feedback: Rectangles contribute CONGRUENT diagonals; a non-square rectangle's diagonals cross at a slant.

options.label: It's a square-only property with no parent
options.feedback: Every rhombus — square or leaning — has perpendicular diagonals; the square just inherits it.

options.label: The trapezoid branch
options.feedback: Trapezoids sit on a different branch entirely (one parallel pair) and promise nothing about diagonal angles.

steps.body: The **square** is where the two upgrade paths meet: a parallelogram that is BOTH a rectangle (all right angles) AND a rhombus (all sides congruent). It doesn't need its own property list — it inherits both, in full: congruent diagonals from the rectangle side, perpendicular angle-bisecting diagonals from the rhombus side.
A square is a rhombus you cannot escape.

predict.prompt: Three corners are pinned at (0,0), (5,0) and (5,5). How many places can the fourth corner go and still make a square?

options.label: Exactly one — the other three corners have already decided it
Two — one on each side of the diagonal
Four — one for each rotation of the square

predict.reveal: Exactly one. Three corners of a square leave no freedom at all for the fourth — every other position breaks either a side length or a right angle. Place it and watch the name snap to "a square" at one spot and nowhere else.

widget.prompt: Pinned at (0,0), (5,0) and (5,5). Place the fourth corner to make a square.
widget.successFeedback: (0, 5) — and look at what the readout says: all four sides 5, both diagonals 7.07. It satisfies the rhombus test (all sides equal) AND the rectangle test (diagonals equal), which is precisely why a square IS both. You did not have to memorise that; the shape refused to be anything less.
widget.sideFeedback: Not in A's column, so the sides cannot all come out equal. A square needs four sides of 5.
widget.angleFeedback: Right column, wrong height — the four sides are not all 5 yet, so it is not even a rhombus.

cml.actionGoal: Move one vertex while side, diagonal, angle, and family evidence update together.

steps.body: The angle-bisecting power gets specific in a square: each 90° corner splits into two **45°** halves, so a diagonal turns the square into two 45-45-90 triangles — the special right triangle from the trig course. Side s gives diagonal s√2, and diagonal d gives side d/√2. Direction decides multiply or divide.

explanationVariants: diagonal = 5√2 ≈ 7.07 — the 45-45-90 hypotenuse rule with legs 5.
Multiply the side by √2 going toward the hypotenuse: 5 × 1.414 ≈ 7.07.

widget.prompt: A square has side 5. Its diagonal (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 = 5 + 5 adds two sides walking around the corner — the diagonal cuts straight across: 5√2 ≈ 7.07.
3.54 ≈ 5 ÷ √2 divides — the wrong direction. Side to diagonal MULTIPLIES by √2: ≈ 7.07.
25 = 5² is the square's AREA. The diagonal is a length: 5√2 ≈ 7.07.

explanationVariants: side = 10 ÷ √2 ≈ 7.07 — shrinking from hypotenuse back to leg divides.

widget.prompt: A square's DIAGONAL is 10. Its side (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 14.14 = 10√2 multiplies — producing a side LONGER than the diagonal, impossible (the diagonal is the hypotenuse). Divide: ≈ 7.07.
5 = 10 ÷ 2 halves — but √2 ≈ 1.414 is the true ratio, not 2. 10/√2 ≈ 7.07.
100 = 10² squares the diagonal — that's twice the AREA, not the side. 10/√2 ≈ 7.07.

steps.body: Watch the hierarchy's one-way arrows. **Every square is a rectangle** (it has the right angles) and **every square is a rhombus** (it has the equal sides) — but neither claim reverses. A rectangle needn't have equal sides; a rhombus needn't have right angles. “Is-a” flows UP the family tree, never down.

explanationVariants: Squares satisfy the rhombus definition (four congruent sides), so every square IS a rhombus; a leaning rhombus fails the square's right-angle test.
Up the tree: always. Down the tree: only sometimes.

options.label: Every square is a rhombus, but not every rhombus is a square
options.feedback: A square's four equal sides meet the rhombus definition; a rhombus leaning at 70° flunks squarehood.

options.label: Every rhombus is a square, but not every square is a rhombus
options.feedback: Reversed: the rhombus is the BROADER class. Squares are the rhombi that also manage right angles.

options.label: Squares and rhombi are disjoint categories
options.feedback: Far from disjoint — every square lives inside the rhombus family. The families nest; they don't split.

options.label: The two terms are synonyms
options.feedback: Rhombi outnumber squares: any slanted equal-sided parallelogram is a rhombus that is no square.

widget.prompt: A square's diagonal meets its sides at what angle, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 90° is where the two DIAGONALS meet each other. Each diagonal meets a SIDE at half a corner: 45°.
60° belongs to equilateral-triangle country — a square's corner is 90°, and the diagonal halves it: 45°.

hints: A rectangle already guarantees right angles — what's still missing for squarehood?
The rhombus half of the package: all four sides congruent (consecutive sides equal suffices).
Alternatively, in diagonal language: a rectangle whose diagonals are ALSO perpendicular.
explanationVariants: A rectangle needs the side condition (consecutive sides congruent) — or, equivalently, perpendicular diagonals — to be certified a square.
Right angles are in hand; equal sides (or the perpendicular-diagonal signature) closes the deal.

widget.prompt: A quadrilateral is known to be a rectangle. Which ONE additional fact certifies it's a square?

options.label: Two consecutive sides are congruent
options.feedback: Opposite sides already match (parallelogram), so one equal consecutive pair spreads to all four — rectangle + rhombus = square.

options.label: Its diagonals are congruent
options.feedback: Congruent diagonals come FREE with every rectangle — no new information. Add equal consecutive sides (or perpendicular diagonals).

options.label: Its opposite sides are parallel
options.feedback: Already guaranteed — every rectangle is a parallelogram. The missing ingredient is the equal-sides condition.

options.label: It has four right angles
options.feedback: That's the rectangle's own definition, already in the bank. The upgrade needs congruent consecutive sides.

takeaways: Square = rectangle ∩ rhombus: all right angles AND all congruent sides.
Diagonals inherit everything: congruent, perpendicular, mutually bisecting, corner-splitting into 45°s.
s√2 converts side to diagonal; divide by √2 to go back.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: quadrilaterals that AREN'T parallelograms — trapezoids and kites.
